title: Seseo, ceceo y distinción
subtitle: Z and soft c: "th" in Spain, s almost everywhere else

lessons.title: Distinción: the Spanish "th"
lessons.goal: Pronounce z and c (before e, i) as [θ] the way most of Spain does, and keep s as s.

tip.title: Tongue between the teeth, no voice
tip.body: In most of Spain, z (zumo, azul, vez) and c before e or i (cena, cine, hacer) are pronounced [θ], the sound of English "th" in "think" — never the buzzing "th" of "this". Put the tip of your tongue lightly between your upper and lower front teeth and blow air through without using your voice. The letter s stays a real s: tongue tip up behind the upper teeth, often a little further back than an English s, which gives Castilian s its slightly "whistly" sound. Keeping the two apart is called distinción, and it lets Spaniards hear a difference between casa (house) and caza (hunt), or coser (to sew) and cocer (to boil). It is not a lisp: a lisp turns every s into th, while distinción only uses th where the spelling has z or ce/ci. A word with both sounds is good practice: "sucio" = su-θio, "cerveza" = θer-be-θa. Final -d in words like "Madrid" or "usted" is soft and in parts of central Spain can sound close to [θ] too; you don't need to copy that.

phrases.note: Spain: θin-co θer-be-θas. Three θ sounds, one final s.

phrases.t: La plaza está cerca del centro.
phrases.n: The square is near the centre.
Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

lessons.title: Seseo: the other standard
lessons.goal: Recognise seseo as fully standard, understand homophones it creates, and know what ceceo is.

tip.title: Seseo is not a mistake
tip.body: In all of Latin America, the Canary Islands and much of Andalusia, z and ce/ci are simply pronounced s: "cerveza" = ser-be-sa, "gracias" = gra-sias. This is called seseo, and it is the pronunciation of the vast majority of Spanish speakers; it is completely standard, used by newsreaders, teachers and presidents. With seseo, casa and caza, coser and cocer, ciento and siento sound exactly the same, and context does the work, just as with English "right" and "write". Choose one system and be consistent: if you learn Spanish for Mexico or Colombia, use seseo; for Madrid, distinción. Both are understood everywhere, but you must recognise both. The s of seseo is usually made with the tongue tip down behind the lower teeth, like an English s. Ceceo is the opposite: in some parts of Andalusia, especially in rural areas, many speakers pronounce s as well as z/ce/ci with a th-like sound, so "casa" can sound like "caza". It is a real regional feature, but it carries less social prestige than seseo or distinción, so learners are best advised to recognise it rather than imitate it. Spelling note: speakers with seseo have to memorise which words take z/c and which take s.

phrases.note: "siento" has s everywhere; with seseo it sounds like "ciento".
With seseo, "la caza" sounds like "la casa": context tells you it's hunting.
Spain: θie-rra; seseo: sie-rra, the same as "sierra" (mountain range).
Spain: ne-θe-si-to θien; seseo: ne-se-si-to sien.

stress.note: Spain: θien-to θin-cuen-ta; seseo: sien-to sin-cuen-ta.
Two plain s sounds in every accent.

story.title: ¿Casa o caza?
story.intro: A Spaniard, a Mexican and a Colombian notice that two words sound the same for two of them.

lines.name: Javier
lines.t: Este fin de semana mi padre se va de caza.
lines.n: This weekend my father is going hunting.

lines.name: Dalia
lines.t: ¿De caza o de casa? Para mí suenan igual.
lines.n: Hunting or home? To me they sound the same.

lines.name: Javier
lines.t: De caza, con zeta. Va al campo a cazar conejos.
lines.n: Hunting, with a z. He's going to the countryside to hunt rabbits.

lines.name: Gonzalo
lines.t: En Colombia decimos las dos palabras con ese, y el contexto lo aclara todo.
lines.n: In Colombia we say both words with an s, and the context makes everything clear.

lines.name: Dalia
lines.t: En México también. Y es un español perfectamente correcto.
lines.n: In Mexico too. And it's perfectly correct Spanish.

lines.name: Javier
lines.t: Claro que sí. En Canarias y en buena parte de Andalucía también hay seseo.
lines.n: Of course. In the Canary Islands and much of Andalusia there's seseo too.

lines.name: Gonzalo
lines.t: Pues a mí me encanta oír la zeta de ustedes en España.
lines.n: Well, I love hearing your z in Spain.

questions.q: ¿Cómo dicen "caza" en Colombia y en México?
questions.n: How do they say "caza" in Colombia and Mexico?
Where is there seseo in Spain?
t: En Canarias y en buena parte de Andalucía
